contract_groups.title: Exact168–175 fields, framing and names
contract: Header is4B: size BE16 includes header, then type BE16. Official message IDs168–175 are retained; no private envelope or requestID is added.
SET168: flags BE32 at4,value BE64 at8,two NUL strings at16; GET169/WATCH172: two NUL strings at4; VALUE170: rawUID BE32 at4,value BE64 at8,two NUL strings at16.
END171,DISCONNECT174,CONFIRM175 are exact4B. WATCH_VALUE173 is exact24B: flags BE32@4,wid BE32@8,reserved BE32@12,value BE64@16. Producer reserved is0.

Names are opaque case-sensitive byte strings, not forced UTF8. Exactly two terminators consume the names region; caller interior NUL or wire missing/extra/trailing name data is not a new selector. Header size is16-bit; configured resource refusal is separate from format.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Exchange independently observed request/response frames through actual client/service boundaries.
expected_observations: Observe exact type/length/endian/offsets and original opaque names; no synthetic terminator, UTF8 rewrite or private fields.
Verify exact fixed-size terminal frames and retained raw flags/UID/WID/reserved fields before interpreting them.
variants: all168–175 schemas
empty/ASCII/nonUTF8/case-distinct names
header/fixed-payload/name boundary and malformed complete frame

contract_groups.title: Global SET arithmetic, persistence replacement and UID
contract_groups.boundary: live service state visible through GET/WATCH
contract: Absolute SET stores unsigned64 value; relative SET interprets value bits as signed64 delta. Existing negative subtraction clamps at0; positive overflow stores modulo2^64 (C diagnoses but continues).
A new nonpositive relative row is0/unset. Existing unset row becomes set on first SET. Unknown SET bits do not change known-bit behavior.

Persistence is replaced on every actual SET using flags&2, including an unchanged numeric value. VALUE high-bit31 marks persistence; low31-bit UID stays stable for that row during the live service session. Do not require stable UID across restart or wrapping UID allocator behavior.
Native update(0) is a separate complete no-op: no admitted mutation/connection or persistence change. Raw relative-zero SET may replace persistence and establish an unset row.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Create counters, update through both implementations and inspect resulting GET, raw UID and relevant WATCH outputs.
expected_observations: Observed value, low UID and current persistence flag agree after every admitted update.
Relative-zero native no-op emits its distinct CLI terminal and cannot be counted as a processing-confirmed mutation.
variants: absolute0/u64MAX
positive/negative delta and clamp/wrap boundary
first nonpositive-relative/unset transition
same-value persistence toggle and unknown flags
native zero no-op contrasted with actual raw zero SET

contract_groups.title: GET selectors, VALUE identity and actual END
contract: Empty subsystem and name independently mean wildcard for GET; nonempty names match exact bytes. SET/WATCH empty names are literal.
GET yields every matching row, including zero/unset watch-created rows, then exactly one header-only END even for zero matches.

GET has no wire requestID. Only that original request successful END completes it; EOF, timeout, local cancellation or source loss do not become success. UIDs identify rows within a session, not authentication.

Consumers preserve exact selector bytes and numeric values. CLI display is lossy UTF8 plus exact byte arrays; count is actual wholly emitted rows, not an assumed number or old10000 cap. Listing order is not added as a new cross-implementation requirement.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Use exact/independent wildcard selectors over missing, single and multiple rows and follow original stream to real END.
expected_observations: Match original name/value/persistence/UID fields and complete row set; empty selection has END0.
Consumer requires actual END and zero exit; partial rows followed by later failure never count as complete listing.
variants: zero/one/many rows
all-subsystems/all-names/one-axis wildcards
unset row and opaque native name rendering

contract_groups.title: WATCH WID, initial values and true changes
contract: WATCH has exact literal names, no ACK or END. WIDs enumerate actual wire registrations per connection from0; WATCH_VALUE carries absolute value, flags0/2, reserved0.
Initial nonzero current value notifies; initial0 (including set0) is silent. Watch on missing row creates zero/unset row visible through GET.

First SET on a watch-created unset row can notify0. Later equal values are suppressed per subscription; changing only persistence does not notify. A real numeric change reflects the new persistence in subsequent notification.
Closing one connection removes only its watches/queued effects, retaining global values and other connections.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Register multiple actual watches, mutate from a separate client and independently observe exact notification fields.
expected_observations: No fabricated initial zero, registration ACK or END. WID and selector stay bound to the original subscription/connection.
Only required numeric/initial-set changes notify; other watchers remain correct after one owner retires.
variants: missing/zero/nonzero initial values
first zero SET then duplicate0

contract_groups.title: GET cancellation, aborted iteration and late replies
contract_groups.boundary: original public API/IPC operation and connection epoch
contract: Explicit cancel of queued GET removes it. Cancel of current GET suppresses its rows and continuation but leaves the original stream draining until its END; there is no wire CANCEL or requestID.

Iterator AbortIteration suppresses remaining rows but is distinct from explicit cancellation: the ordinary END can still yield original successful completion. Connection loss completes a non-aborted original GET with failure, never a new query success.

A cancelled/stale original ID cannot capture later replies or authorize cancellation in another instance. A later queued GET is not assigned the cancelled stream late VALUE/END. C same-stack destroy prohibition is handled by Rust callback/lifetime API rather than copying an unsafe ABI.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Cancel a queued/current original GET or abort its iterator, then allow actual late stream bytes and a distinct later query.
expected_observations: Cancelled original has no rows/continuation after cancellation; late END drains its stream without completing the later GET.
Iterator-aborted rows remain suppressed but real END/loss retains the corresponding success/failure distinction.
variants: queued versus current cancel
iterator abort versus explicit cancel

contract_groups.title: Logical WATCH cancellation and new physical WID mapping
contract_groups.boundary: original public API/IPC operation and connection epoch
contract: watch_cancel removes the local live subscription; no wire UNWATCH exists. Late old WID notifications must not reach a cancelled callback, and ordinary connection close releases server registrations.

Reconnect may re-register only live logical watches, with fresh connection-local WIDs determined by new actual registration order. Stable logical subscription identity is distinct from each physical WID and old connection epoch.

Cancel holes and logical slot reuse must not cause old callbacks or route another selector notification to the wrong owner. Fixed C client has a source-predicted hole/reconnect indexing defect; preserve official wire WIDs and correct logical ownership instead of reproducing that defect.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Register two real watches, cancel an early registration, reconnect the same logical owner, and mutate the remaining exact selector.
expected_observations: Cancelled callback stays silent; surviving logical watch receives its own actual absolute value with the new physical WID.
No invented ACK or retained old-epoch authorization; old notifications cannot be rebound through slot reuse.
variants: cancel-before-connect and cancel-live
late cancelled-WID notification

contract_groups.title: Connection loss, pending intent and unknown exposed mutations
contract_groups.boundary: original public API/IPC operation and connection epoch
contract: Client loss distinguishes the current GET, live logical subscriptions, still-queued mutation intent and a SET/UPDATE already exposed to the old connection. Current non-aborted GET fails; pending independent intent may remain eligible for the owner documented retry path.

An exposed mutation may already have changed the service when reply/connection is lost. Reconnect cannot manufacture old processing confirmation or blindly replay an unknown SET/UPDATE into a new epoch.

Native destroy receipt retains discarded queued mutations plus unconfirmed mutation/persistent counts across original epochs. A later epoch confirmation may confirm only its own current work, not erase unknown old history.
No automatic exactly-once or durable claim is inferred from C void setter APIs, local MQ acceptance, local whole-write, reconnect, or a new independent GET.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Lose the actual old connection before transmission versus after a mutation may have been written; reconnect only according to retained native intent.
expected_observations: Preserve original typed loss/transport cause and unknown mutation accounting. No old confirmation or automatic exposed mutation replay enters a new epoch.
A new independent observation is labelled as such; it does not retroactively prove old operation processing.
variants: unexposed queued intent vs exposed SET/relative update
current GET fails while live WATCH can re-register

contract_groups.title: sync_first destruction and actual processing receipt
contract_groups.boundary: original public API/IPC operation and connection epoch
contract: Public destroy(sync_first) means pending SET requests should be completed. Active C defers only when sync_first, a real MQ exists and its non-transmitted length is positive; otherwise destruction discards remaining work, not processing confirmation.

Deferred destroy suppresses queued GET/WATCH work, drains its admitted ordering, sends original DISCONNECT and waits for matching confirmation under the already-selected five-times-backoff deadline. Do not require a C scheduler/task implementation or callback ABI.

Immediate discard, deadline, loss, physical drop and successful processing confirmation remain distinct terminal outcomes. No later retry renews original destruction deadline or turns discarded/unknown mutation counts into zero.

Normal finite SET requires ProcessingConfirmed with all discarded/unconfirmed fields zero. Cleanup must continue same started destruction, preserve original/independent causes and physically release resources without substituting Drop for a receipt.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Begin one native destruction with and without pending original mutation work and observe the actual source terminal.
expected_observations: Only matching actual confirmation plus complete original accounting permits confirmed SET output.
Discard/deadline/loss/drop remain non-success and original deadline/cause is retained through cleanup.
variants: sync_first=false/immediate cleanup
sync_first=true with pending envelope versus no pending envelope
missing/late/foreign confirmation

contract_groups.title: DISCONNECT processing confirmation is separate from durable save
contract: DISCONNECT174 produces exact CONFIRM175 after preceding request handling on that connection. The active official handler does not call save/fsync despite its stale sync-to-disk comment.

Confirmation proves IPC ordering, not independently observed durable filesystem commit. Local write, destroy/drop, EOF or any other terminal outcome cannot substitute for the matching actual confirmation.
Service need not close the connection merely on receiving DISCONNECT; caller lifecycle owns physical retirement. Graceful service shutdown is the separate persistence boundary.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Order a mutation and barrier on the same real connection; separately shut down/restart for durability evidence.
expected_observations: Require exact actual CONFIRM and complete original mutation accounting before confirmed output.
A separately observed restart is required for retained values; ACK alone grants no persistence credit.
variants: valid barrier after update
missing/wrong/extra-payload confirmation or connection loss
clean shutdown distinct from IPC processing

contract_groups.title: Public SET dump, restart and empty removal
contract: Canonical saved database is concatenated official absolute persistent SET168 frames, flags2, values and two NUL strings. It has no private header, UID, watcher or connection state.
Only persistent rows survive a real graceful stop/restart; transient values must first be observed present, then absent afterward. Saved values can be loaded by either implementation.
An empty persistent set removes the previous database, or leaves it absent; it does not preserve stale counters in a private empty wrapper.

Official loader applies complete ordinary SET semantics in order; Rust production uses replay into a fresh unpublished candidate and refuses malformed/truncated/over-capacity load rather than advertising a partial empty core. The strict canonical-only SDK restore is a separate API.
Filesystem errors preserve actual stage/cause/uncertain namespace-commit outcome; graceful-save success is not a claim about power-loss durability.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Observe persistent and transient counters before an actual zero-exit service stop; inspect public bytes and perform real restart/cross-load.
expected_observations: Persistent value/flag survives both loading directions; transient was proven present before absence afterward.
No UID/watch metadata enters public artifact; no-persistent shutdown removes old file and restart has empty result.
Broken load/save never becomes a valid empty authoritative observation or passing persistence result.
variants: canonical C→Rust and Rust→C loads
duplicate/relative/unknown-bit SET replay within valid SET stream

contract_groups.title: Malformed streams, owner isolation and resource refusal
contract: Fixed-size and names integrity checks apply before dispatch. Partial EOF, malformed lengths/names and exhausted selected capacity may terminate that original session; they do not produce END or processing confirmation.
A bad/slow connection must not be reported as successful or corrupt independent healthy clients and original global state. Retiring that connection removes its watches/notifications.

Rust explicitly bounds frames, pending bytes, sessions, rows, name storage, watchers and queued effects. Capacity/error policy is distinct from the65535-byte public format and must be recorded for a selected profile.

Unknown-message default C MQ handling has a known unmatched-handler pause/soft-shutdown defect; diagnose it separately rather than requiring Rust to reproduce it or converting timeout/kill to a successful close. TOLERANT is a separately selected common-service profile.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Open a healthy independent client alongside a bounded malformed/partial/over-capacity session and observe both real outcomes.
expected_observations: Only actual terminal/error and resource outcomes are recorded; healthy state/query remains usable.
No fake completion or relaxed framing results from capacity/timeout; unknown-C variance is separate diagnostic evidence.
variants: invalid fixed-size/names/header and partial EOF
configured input/output/session capacity boundary
bounded slow/stopped receiver with healthy independent client

contract_groups.title: Configured Unix/TCP and selected admission policy
contract: Normal service reads statistics UNIXPATH/PORT/BINDTO/DISABLEV6; configured clients use UNIXPATH/HOSTNAME/PORT on the same native Resolver/clock domain. At least one usable endpoint is required.
Default installed statistics configuration selects local Unix path and DATABASE with localhost ACL defaults. An explicitly selected TCP profile uses the same168–175 protocol, not peer/P2P transport.

Configured IPv4/IPv6 allow-list must match (or be absent), and deny-list takes precedence. Unix UID/GID admission and filesystem policy are selected deployment conditions; Rust uses actual kernel credentials with UID precedence, then GID/group membership.

Denied, malformed, unavailable or failed endpoint/admission outcomes are real failures, not authenticated STATISTICS peers or successful operations. Do not equate implementation-specific credential checks with a new wire authentication schema.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Select the actual normal configuration and independently observe Unix/TCP connection, allowed/denied identities or addresses, and actual IPC results.
expected_observations: Same public fields/semantics hold on each explicitly selected endpoint; configured denial is observed before core admission.
Record platform/identity/address capability and selected limits. Unsupported/missing capability remains unverified, never a fabricated pass.
variants: default private Unix with selected UID/GID policy
configured IPv4/IPv6 TCP, HOSTNAME/BINDTO/PORT

contract_groups.title: Normal configured GET/SET/WATCH and bounded native output
contract: Normal get/set/watch routes through PROGRAM before outer stdout lock/UTF8 conversion; - selects configured endpoint, explicit Unix path disables TCP fallback. Finite GNUNET_ARGS prefix defaults permit explicit common option override before endpoint; signed relative value and suffix flags remain literal command data.

GET stdout retains actual value, UID, boolean persistence, displayed selector plus exact bytes; terminal count is wholly written rows after original real END. SET emits confirmed only from original complete processing receipt; zero-relative has distinct noop.

One original10s finite command bound covers admission/stream/terminal output; stalled output retains one row and original native cursor. WATCH has no synthesized ACK/zero; it retains its continuous original subscription and row bounds.

Signal/parent stop, clock/Resolver loss, output/flush/native failure retain actual original and independent cleanup causes. Cancel only the still-owned original GET/WATCH; retire same native handle then Resolver. Synchronous OS write/flush cannot be preempted; late return fails.

necessary_case_group.stimulus: Invoke ordinary configured commands and observe actual data/terminal/exit and cause, with bounded output interruption as applicable.
expected_observations: Do not treat emitted terminal alone as whole success: require zero exit and completed flush/retirement.
No fallback fake client, second mutation owner, unbounded row aggregate or destroyed-as-confirmed result.

real SET receipt vs zero-relative noop

reference_variances.fact: Service emits flags2 but fixed C WATCH callback interprets bit31. Rust follows active producer wire flags2 and preserves raw fields; numerical C WATCH value alone does not validate persistence.

C cancel leaves NULL array slot; reconnect resends only live entries without compaction; server restarts physical WIDs from0; incoming C dispatch still indexes old array by WID. Cancelled early slot can therefore suppress/misroute surviving watch after reconnect. Rust rebuilds physical WID→live logical mapping and must not reproduce wrong ownership.
MQ inject handles SYSERR but not unmatched NO; service sets needs_continue before injection. Unsupported-type pause/soft-shutdown timeout is not a successful close or a Rust requirement.
Active DISCONNECT handler only sends confirmation; actual save is shutdown. Do not elevate stale sync-to-disk comment to fsync ACK requirement.

C signed -delta at INT64_MIN is undefined; save asserts frame size<UINT16_MAX and UID allocator eventually overlaps persistence bit. Rust must retain signed64 format/safe arithmetic and explicit resource refusal, not emulate undefined behavior/assertion/UID corruption. Positive unsigned overflow has defined wrap and is separately required.
